summary.oneLiner: Alembic Limited is a Vadodara-based company operating two distinct businesses - real estate development and leasing under the Alembic City campus, and manufacture of bulk drugs (APIs and pharmaceutical intermediates), with real estate contributing the large majority of turnover.
summary.business: The Company develops and leases residential and commercial real estate, principally the Alembic City township in Vadodara, comprising premium low-rise duplex apartments, villas, apartments and commercial/office space, alongside a mixed-use art and community district. Separately, its Bulk Drugs business manufactures pharmaceutical intermediates and generic APIs and undertakes job-work manufacturing for pharmaceutical company customers.

currentContext.strengths: Integrated township model combining residential, commercial and leasing-led recurring income within the Alembic City campus|Vadodara location benefits from an established industrial ecosystem, positioning within the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor framework, and improving regional transport connectivity|New commercial office building achieved ~90% of leasable area covered by lease commitments upon completion, indicating strong occupier demand|Alembic Art District drives footfall and place-making, supporting the township's distinct market positioning|In Bulk Drugs, improved product yields, better utility optimisation and reduced dependence on imported raw materials enabled higher job-work volumes despite a limited product portfolio
currentContext.strategies: Real Estate Business to be guided by calibrated execution, selective development and expansion of leasing-led recurring income|Continued focus on the Vadodara market and progression of the integrated Alembic City campus (residential, commercial and community-oriented development)|Building depth in the leasing portfolio and mixed-use ecosystem (commercial office space, Alembic Art District) to diversify towards recurring income|In Bulk Drugs, sustaining operations through focused efforts (yield improvement, utility optimisation, reduced import dependence) within a limited product portfolio, with continuous strategic evaluation of the segment given an uncertain long-term outlook|Selective workforce structuring to maintain operational efficiency, with flexibility measures for eligible roles retained to support organisational agility|Bulk Drugs business migrated from SAP ECC to SAP S/4HANA during the year, continuing to strengthen system-based controls and process integration|The Company maintains a formal Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015, disclosed on its website, and a Nomination and Remuneration Policy under Section 178 of the Act/Regulation 19 covering remuneration for managerial personnel, KMP, senior management and directors. Declaration of dividend for FY26 was placed before shareholders as ordinary business at the AGM.
currentContext.expansion: Real estate expansion during FY26 centred on the Alembic City campus in Vadodara, comprising residential, commercial and community-oriented development. Within the residential portfolio, VEDA-II (a gated community project completed in FY25) achieved full sales towards the end of FY26, The Gardens (a niche duplex apartment project) was completed during FY26 and achieved full sales, and Park Crescent (3BHK/4BHK configurations, launched the previous year) continued to see encouraging homebuyer response. On the commercial/leasing side, a new commercial office building whose construction had commenced the previous year was completed during FY26, with approximately 90% of its leasable area covered by lease commitments; the Alembic Art District (including Space Studio, run by the Alembic CSR Foundation) continued to build out the campus's mixed-use, community-oriented character. The Bulk Drugs (API) business did not report any new capacity or plant expansion during the year; it instead focused on yield improvement, utility optimisation and reduced import dependence within its existing, limited product portfolio. Named-disclosure capital-commitment notes (both standalone, page 119, and consolidated, page 168) reported the capital expenditure contracted for but not recognised as liabilities as a dash/nil for the periods shown, i.e. no quantified capital commitment was disclosed as outstanding at either balance-sheet date.
currentContext.mdna: Indian economy remained resilient in FY26 (Economic Survey estimated real GDP growth of 7.4%), with private consumption and investment supporting real estate demand via urbanisation, infrastructure spending and end-user preference for ownership|Residential demand showed resilience with a shift towards premium and higher-value housing, though multiple external factors caused a drop in overall demand towards the end of the financial year|Office and mixed-use real estate continued to see occupier demand support from business expansion, infrastructure improvements and growing preference for integrated work environments|Tier II/III cities (including Gujarat/Vadodara) continued to benefit from urbanisation, connectivity and decentralisation, but affordability pressures and a cautious supply environment moderated housing sales and launches across several Tier II cities|Vadodara specifically benefits from an established industrial ecosystem, its location within the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor framework, and improving regional transport connectivity|Medium-term demand outlook for Vadodara and other Tier-II markets remains good, but near-term conditions require discipline in pricing, product positioning and inventory management|Bulk Drugs (API) business constrained by a limited product portfolio, continued competitive intensity in several molecules, and customer concentration; the low-margin job-work segment remained subdued in scale|VEDA-II (gated community project completed in FY2025) achieved full sales towards the end of FY26|The Gardens (niche duplex apartment project) attained completion during FY26 and achieved full sales|Park Crescent (residential project with 3BHK/4BHK configurations, launched in the previous year) continued to receive encouraging response from homebuyers|New commercial office building at Alembic City completed during FY26 with approximately 90% of leasable area covered by lease commitments

risks.risk: Uncertain long-term outlook for the Bulk Drugs (API) segment
risks.note: Management explicitly flagged that despite focused efforts sustaining operations, 'the long-term outlook for this segment remains uncertain, necessitating continuous strategic evaluation' - implying the segment's continuation is not assured over the long term.

risks.risk: Limited product portfolio and customer concentration in Bulk Drugs
risks.note: The API manufacturing business 'continued to operate in limited space due to constraints of a limited product portfolio, continued competitive intensity in several molecules and customer concentration', constraining its ability to scale.

risks.risk: Subdued, low-margin job-work segment within Bulk Drugs
risks.note: The scale of the low-margin job-work segment 'remained subdued', limiting the segment's contribution even where volumes improved marginally.

risks.risk: Near-term real estate demand softness and market selectivity
risks.note: Despite resilient residential demand overall, 'towards the end of the financial year, multiple external factors led to a drop in overall demand', and demand conditions 'became more selective across markets and price segments', requiring pricing and inventory discipline.

risks.risk: Affordability pressures and cautious supply in Tier II/III markets
risks.note: Housing sales and launches moderated across several Tier II cities during the year 'as rising prices and shrinking affordable supply affected volumes', a structural constraint on the geography the Company depends on (Vadodara/Gujarat).

The Company's real estate business is concentrated on the Vadodara/Gujarat market (the Alembic City campus), making its performance sensitive to the specific demand and regulatory conditions of that single Tier-II market.

The Company 'remained watchful of statutory developments in labour and employment matters, including the implementation of the four Labour Codes and the related regulatory developments thereunder', an unresolved compliance/cost risk.

The Board's Report cautions that 'certain statements in the [MD&A] report may be forward-looking' and that 'many factors may affect the actual results, which could be different from what the Directors envisage in terms of future performance and outlook.'
